meta.title: Handling of Corrosive and Hazardous Chemicals

sections.purpose: To establish safe practices for the storage, transfer, use, and disposal of corrosive, toxic, flammable, and reactive chemicals in pharmacy laboratories to protect personnel and prevent accidents.
sections.scope: Applicable to all chemistry, pharmaceutics, pharmacognosy, and research laboratories where hazardous chemicals are utilized.
procedure: Consult the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for any chemical before handling it to understand its specific hazards, personal protective equipment requirements, and spill response protocol.
Wear appropriate PPE including chemical splash goggles, a buttoned lab coat, long pants, closed-toe shoes, and chemical-resistant gloves.
Perform all operations involving volatile, toxic, corrosive, or foul-smelling chemicals inside a certified chemical fume hood. Verify the fume hood blower is operating before starting.
Transport chemicals in secondary containment buckets or carriers to prevent accidental spills due to dropped containers.
When diluting concentrated acids, always add the acid to water slowly with constant stirring. Never add water to concentrated acid, as it can cause violent boiling and acid projection.
Pour chemicals carefully, keeping the container opening away from the body and others.
Use pipette fillers or bulbs for measuring liquid reagents. Never use mouth suction to pipette any chemical.
Label all secondary containers (beakers, flasks, reagent bottles) immediately with the chemical name, concentration, date, and appropriate hazard warnings.
Store hazardous chemicals in compatible groups as per chemical compatibility guidelines (e.g., store acids separately from bases, flammables separately from oxidizers).
Keep all chemical storage cabinet doors closed and locked when not in use.
Report any spill, exposure, or near-miss to the Laboratory In-charge immediately and follow the spill control protocol.
Dispose of chemical waste in designated, clearly labeled waste carboys. Never pour hazardous chemicals down the laboratory sink.
precautions: Never mix incompatible chemicals (e.g., concentrated nitric acid and organic solvents) as this can lead to violent explosions or toxic gas release.
Do not heat flammable solvents using an open flame; use a water bath, oil bath, or heating mantle.
Ensure eyewash stations and safety showers are unobstructed and tested weekly.
Avoid direct skin or eye contact with all chemicals; wash hands immediately if contact occurs.
Never eat, drink, apply cosmetics, or store food in areas where hazardous chemicals are used or stored.
Keep chemical containers closed tightly when not actively dispensing to prevent vapor release.
